therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: androgen deprivation through suppression of luteinizing hormone and testosterone
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: percentage of participants with effective castration rate (testosterone <50 ng/dL) over 25 weeks

results.target_engagement_evidence: Rapid testosterone suppression achieved in median 4 days for TAK-385 vs 3 days for degarelix; LH suppression from baseline 5.838 to 0.388 mIU/mL at week 2
biomarker_changes: PSA reduction: 97.4% reduction at week 25 for TAK-385 vs 96.3% for degarelix
Testosterone recovery: 48% of TAK-385 patients recovered to >280 ng/dL vs 13% for degarelix
Prostate size reduction: 25.1% for TAK-385 vs 27.2% for degarelix
LH recovery faster with TAK-385: 9.441 mIU/mL at week 37 vs 1.036 for degarelix
subgroup_findings: PSA response ≥50%: 64/65 TAK-385 patients vs 37/38 degarelix patients
PSA response ≥90%: 36/65 TAK-385 patients vs 18/38 degarelix patients
safety_signals: More TEAEs with TAK-385: 56/65 vs 37/38 for degarelix
Fewer SAEs with TAK-385: 1/65 vs 3/38 for degarelix
Hormonal treatment-related symptoms increased similarly in both groups
results.dose_information: TAK-385 120 mg tablet daily vs Degarelix 80 mg injection
